ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (Articles L. 561-2 et seq. for AML/CFT obligations; Articles L. 561-1 et seq. for beneficial ownership identification), Ordonnance n° 2020-306 du 25 mars 2020, Décret n° 2017-924 du 6 mai 2017 relatif à l'identification des bénéficiaires effectifs, updated by subsequent ordinances and Banque de France implementing regulations

Competent authority in country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, EU and domestic (Tracfin, Banque de France) screening standards including senior official lists, sanctions designations and adverse media checks

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Infogreffe RCS Portal (greffe du tribunal de commerce)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirement for French language using Latin alphabet; no transliteration permitted for standard corporate names
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying unauthorized banking or insurance activities
Sensitive terms such as 'assurance', 'réassurance', 'captif' or 'réassureur' requiring prior ACPR authorization
Terms restricted under general company law (e.g., 'banque', 'crédit' without ministerial approval)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Administrative appeal to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within two months of rejection notice; subsequent judicial review before the Président du Tribunal de Commerce or Tribunal Administratif if required

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Administrative virtual offices permissible for SAS formation; however, regulated captive reinsurance entities must demonstrate adequate commercial substance and physical presence where required by ACPR licensing conditions
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for pre-incorporation stage; medium for post-licensing ACPR oversight with quantified risk of unannounced on-site inspections for licensed captives

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff plus prevailing market benchmark for regulated entity formation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) Articles L.225-1 to L.225-8, L.227-1 to L.227-20; French Insurance Code (Code des assurances) Articles L.310-1, L.321-1 to L.321-2; Solvency II Directive (2009/138/EC) provisions
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) via InsGroupe / Infogreffe online window
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: M0 declaration (Déclaration de constitution de société) and annexed statutory articles (Statuts)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum under the Commercial Code for an SAS; capital must be fully subscribed and paid at registration. Under the French Insurance Code and Solvency II, a captive reinsurance undertaking must maintain minimum guarantee own funds of at least EUR 2,500,000; funds must be placed in a bank or notarial blocked account until the company obtains its RCS registration and necessary ACPR approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders of the SAS, meeting in constitutive assembly, resolve: (1) the offered subscription to the share capital of EUR 1,000,000 is approved and accepted; the subscribers are authorized to pay the contributions in full before filing. (2) The registered office shall be fixed at 55 Avenue de la Grande Armée, 75116 Paris, France, and the President is instructed to complete any consequential formalities. (3) [Name of first officer] is appointed President and [Name of second officer] is appointed General Manager, each with authority to bind the company under the Articles of the Commercial Code. (4) All statutory and regulatory filings, including the application for ACPR captive reinsurance authorization, are formally approved and executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Statuts and Publish Legal Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaire (optional or mandatory for real estate contributions) and authorized legal gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the société par actions simplifiée (SAS) statuts, including corporate name, purpose, registered office address, capital structure, director powers, governance rules and duration. Submit a legal notice containing the corporate name, form, registered office, capital, and identity of signatories to an approved local legal gazette; obtain proof of publication.
required_dossiers: Notarized or private deed of the statuts
Identity documents of founding shareholders
Legal notice draft for publication in the legal gazette
Bank capital deposit attestation of required paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal gazette rejects the notice, correct the registration details and resubmit. If the statuts contain legal deficiencies, revise and re-execute the deed; if notarization was omitted, engage a notaire to remedy any real-estate contribution irregularity before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a Blocked Capital Account and Obtain Capital Deposit Attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank, notaire, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the name of the company under formation; transfer the share capital by wire from corporate or personal accounts; obtain the attestation de dépôt du capital certifying that funds are fully received and unreleased until registration is complete.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts or power of attorney for the escrow agent
Identification documents of subscribers
Bank account details of the company under formation
Capital payment wire confirmation and source-of-funds evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the attestation, verify the accuracy of wire instructions, confirm currency and amount, provide additional source-of-funds documents, or request a notarial substitute. If the payment is reversed, re-transfer funds and restart the attestation process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit M0 Declaration and File Registration with the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) through Infogreffe online portal or in-person at the competent RCS desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Mandatory Company Declaration (M0), attaching the statuts, capital attestation, legal publication receipt, plus identification and declarations from legal representatives. Pay the required registry fee and obtain a filing receipt. The registry will check compliance with legal requirements and issue approval of the company registration.
required_dossiers: Fully completed M0 form
Signed and dated statuts (original or notarized copy)
Capital deposit attestation issued by bank or notaire
Copy of legal gazette publication (BODACC or proof)
Identity card or passport of the President and General Manager
Declaration of no criminal conviction for the legal representatives
Registered office lease or letting certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a 'demande complémentaire', supply the missing documents within the statutory deadline. If registration is refused, correct the deficiencies, pay any additional fees, and refile; appeal to the President of the Commercial Court under Article R.123-104 of the Commercial Code if the refusal is unjustified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Kbis Extract and Verify Registered Details
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the registry validates the M0 and statutes, request the official Kbis extract certifying the company's legal personality and registration number; verify the registered officers, corporate name, address, and principal business scope; keep the extract for further ACPR application and opening banking facilities.
required_dossiers: Copy of the M0 registration application
Registry acknowledgement of company registration
Final Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains incorrect data, obtain a formal rectification from the registry by submitting the correct documents and an amended M0 declaration. If the registry omits any licensed activity, include the relevant licence approval and request an RCS activity code update.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for ACPR Captive Reinsurance Authorization (Licence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) – 4 Place de Budapest, 75009 Paris, France
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a formal application with the ACPR for consideration as a captive reinsurance undertaking; provide the programme of operations, projected financial situation for three years, solvency capital requirement (SCR) calculation, capital adequacy evidence, governance rules, risk management and internal control systems, AML/CFT measures for enhanced medium-risk operations, and the list of designated board directors / senior managers demonstrating fit-and-proper status.
required_dossiers: ACPR application form (autorisation d'entreprise de réassurance)
Programme d'activité and business plan for the captive reinsurance SPV
Articles of association and Kbis extract
Evidence of paid-up capital and minimum guarantee funds of EUR 2.5 million
Three-year financial projections and run-off plan
AML / CTF policy and procedures (enhanced due diligence medium-risk)
Governance chart with CV of directors / senior officers
Fit-and-proper certificates and declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to ACPR's additional information letters within the imposed short delay, usually 15 working days; if the ACPR opposes or refuses the application, engage in a pre-adversarial exchange, file written observations, and ultimately seek judicial review before the Paris Administrative Court; alternatively, modify the financial plan or capital structure and resubmit the application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: ACPR – Direction des autorisations (Prudential Licensing Department); for outside site accreditation if an office is physically operated, the local municipal authorities (Mairie) may be contacted for continued compliance, but no industrial operational licensing applies to a captive reinsurance SPV.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Agrément d'entreprise de réassurance limité (Captive Reinsurance Undertaking Licence) under Articles L.321-1, L.321-1-1 and R.321-1 of the French Insurance Code

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique / Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) – Environmental assessment clearance for non-industrial undertakings
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – registration not required for a purely financial captive reinsurance SPV; the undertaking conducts only administrative office activities without installations or chemicals use.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for industrial effluents; office waste must comply with municipal waste handling regulations; IT equipment and electronic waste must be disposed of through approved DEEE / electrical equipment take-back schemes in France, and no wastewater or VOC emissions generated beyond standard domestic office loads.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance for the registered office under ERP (Etablissement Recevant du Public) classification, including inspection of emergency exits, smoke detectors, electrical load assessments; occupational health and safety registration with CARSAT; display of internal fire-safety and evacuation instructions; implementation of an employer declaration with the Pôle Emploi / URSSAF for employment and civil liability coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministère de l'Économie et des Finances; online services via impots.gouv.fr and the formalités portal at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SAS, registration starts with electronic submission of incorporation documents to the RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) through the formalities portal. DGFiP assigns the SIREN/SIRET numbers immediately upon dossier validation. The SAS then files a tax registration form and a 'Mise en activité' statement where relevant. For intra-community transactions, DGFiP issues the TVA intracommunautaire number, normally within two to four weeks, after the entity's first VAT return is filed. Non-resident shareholders appoint a fiscal representative registered in France for VAT obligations if the SAS is treated as not fixed in France for VAT purposes, though the domestic SAS itself is a French tax resident entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France operates under a unitary corporate income tax system without a check-the-box partnership election. Relevant elections for the captive reinsurance SAS include: creation of a fiscal group (intégration fiscale) under CGI Article 223A with wholly-owned French subsidiaries; election for VAT grouping under CGI Article 1693-ter and EU VAT Directive provisions; and the statutory election under CGI Article 239 (for limited duration, a newly incorporated SAS may, under strict statutory conditions, elect to be treated as a partnership for income tax purposes). The captive reinsurance activity, however, normally defaults to entity-level corporate income tax at the standard IS rate.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,800 taxable turnover for supplies of goods; EUR 34,400 taxable turnover for supplies of services; lower reduced thresholds apply under the French CGI and the DGFiP aménagements. For financial and insurance/reinsurance-related supplies, a taxable person may also hold a voluntary registration if no threshold is met but input VAT deduction is required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is deploying mandatory e-invoicing for most VAT-taxable persons. Mandates are phased from 1 September 2026 for all entities subject to VAT for B2B invoices, complemented by a mandatory e-reporting regime. Invoices must pass through a certified 'Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP)' or the public portal 'Portail Public de Facturation (PPF)' using the EN 16931 format, with structured data elements (SIREN, VAT ID, transaction codes) and full OCR/XML lodgement. The régime is not a real-time clearance model; data is transmitted in near-real-time business-to-tax-authority reporting without physical digital stamping. The DGFiP archives and reconciles the electronic dataset with VAT returns and customs declarations. For export zero-rating evidence, the e-reporting dataset must include the customs export declaration number, shipping evidence, and counterparty third-party country VAT/GST registration where applicable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods exported from France to non-EU destinations under CGI Article 262-I and EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC Article 146. Reinsurance and captive insurance services may be either outside the scope of French VAT or exempt without credit, depending on whether the counterparty is established in the EU and the actual risk location test is satisfied. Offshore reinsurance for risks located outside the EU can qualify for zero-rate treatment where the services are expressly and directly attributable to non-EU exports and the beneficiary is established outside the EU. The captive reinsurance SAS must maintain contractual risk-certification documentation demonstrating connection to non-French, non-EU underwriting portfolios. For goods-related reinsurance export support, a direct proof of physical export movement is mandatory. The zero-rated supply must be correctly coded on the French e-invoicing platform and reconciled with the customs export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading (or equivalent multimodal transport document)
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment settlement via SWIFT/BIC wire transfer
Shipping and freight documents (packing list, export invoice)
Risk-location certificates for the reinsured underlying risks
Carnet de passage or other transport/insurance supporting documents where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and the Direction Nationale des Enquêtes Fiscales (DNEF) scrutinise export zero-rating claims. Absence of valid customs and financial evidence triggers reassessment of VAT at 20%, addition of late payment penalties at 0.2% per month, a 40% or 80% bad-faith penalty under CGI Article 1729, and civil interest. For fraudulent or fictitious export schemes, criminal tax fraud sanctions apply under CGI Article 1741, including fines up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment for five years, increased when the scheme involves organized fraud or misuse of corporate vehicles. Retrospective clawback extends for the standard three-year tax assessment period, extended to six or ten years for hidden activity or unregistered establishment. Reinsurers may also be held jointly and severally liable with contractual counterparties when the participation in a circular self-billing or export-washing arrangement is established. The captive reinsurance SPV should maintain documentary custody of all export records for at least six years to withstand audit challenge.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, the French Treasury Directorate General (Direction générale du Trésor), and the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR) for regulated reinsurance undertakings. France applies the European Union free-movement-of-capital framework, including Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union Articles 63 to 66, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering, prudential, tax, and reporting controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. France has no general exchange-control approval, mandatory domestic-currency settlement, or general restriction on repatriation of dividends, interest, insurance premiums, claims proceeds, or liquidation proceeds. Cross-border transfers remain subject to bank KYC, beneficial-ownership verification, sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering controls, tax documentation, transfer-pricing support, and prudential asset-allocation rules applicable to an authorized reinsurance undertaking. Distributions by a captive reinsurance company must also comply with French corporate-law distributable-reserve rules, solvency-capital requirements, the approved business plan, Solvency II requirements, and any ACPR supervisory expectation. Payments to related non-residents require arm's-length support, contractual evidence, withholding-tax analysis, and, where relevant, treaty-benefit documentation. A French SAS intended to conduct regulated reinsurance business requires prior legal-form validation because an SAS is not automatically an eligible form for an insurance or reinsurance undertaking under the French Insurance Code. Banking access does not replace the required ACPR authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France, convert export receipts into euros, or repatriate them within a prescribed period. Export proceeds may generally be received and retained in euro or foreign-currency accounts, subject to contractual, tax, accounting, sanctions, and AML obligations. There is no general mandatory conversion ratio. Foreign-currency balances and transactions must be accurately recorded under French accounting rules, with appropriate valuation of monetary items and disclosure where applicable. Cash receipts or payments involving France are subject to applicable cash-payment limits and reporting rules; ordinary banking transfers should therefore be used for material commercial, insurance, capital, and intra-group payments. The entity must separately comply with Intrastat, customs, VAT, statistical, prudential, and Banque de France reporting requirements where applicable. For a reinsurance undertaking, premium, reserve, collateral, and claims accounts must also be consistent with the authorized technical-business model and Solvency II asset-liability governance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
BPCE S.A. and an affiliated Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Épargne institution

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for ancillary payment operations and Low for the primary treasury bank of an authorized captive reinsurer. A licensed European electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide euro payment accounts, SEPA transfers, foreign-exchange execution, and certain collection services under its passported authorization. It cannot accept deposits as a bank, provide unrestricted deposit-taking, hold regulated insurance technical provisions as a substitute for a prudential custodian, or remove the reinsurance undertaking's ACPR, Solvency II, AML, safeguarding, and accounting obligations. Use of an offshore or non-EEA digital EMI requires verification of its local license, EU authorization or passporting status, safeguarding model, correspondent-bank chain, sanctions controls, data-processing arrangements, and ability to support regulated insurance flows. The primary reserve, collateral, and operational accounts should generally be maintained with an EU-authorized credit institution acceptable under the undertaking's investment and risk-management policies.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement for every director to attend a bank branch physically. Remote onboarding may be permitted at the bank's discretion using qualified electronic identification, certified corporate documents, video verification, and reliable beneficial-owner authentication. Banks commonly require at least one live video interview and may require physical attendance or notarized and apostilled documents where the ownership chain is foreign, the entity is newly incorporated, the business is regulated, the source of funds is complex, or the bank cannot independently verify management. The bank will generally require identification of directors, legal representatives, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, the parent group, the captive's insured entities, the reinsurance program, expected countries and currencies, payment counterparties, and the ACPR authorization status. A capital escrow account may be opened before registration, but release normally requires evidence of incorporation and the final corporate registration extract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The entity is described as a captive reinsurer but has no ACPR authorization, no authorization application evidence, or an ineligible legal form.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the legal-form memorandum, French Insurance Code eligibility analysis, ACPR authorization or formal application evidence, approved or submitted business plan, governance chart, fit-and-proper files, actuarial and risk documentation, Solvency II capital assessment, and a written statement that no regulated underwriting will begin before authorization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SAS has a foreign parent, layered ownership, nominee arrangements, trusts, or an ultimate beneficial owner that cannot be identified.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full ownership chart to natural-person beneficial owners, certificates of incorporation and good standing for each intermediate entity, constitutional documents, registers of shareholders and directors, beneficial-owner declarations, trust or foundation instruments where applicable, certified identification, proof of address, and independent corporate-registry extracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of capital, premium funding, collateral, or reserve assets is unclear or inconsistent with the group profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide audited financial statements of the parent and insured group, board-approved funding resolutions, capital contribution agreements, bank statements, loan agreements, tax returns or tax residency evidence where appropriate, source-of-wealth narratives for relevant individuals, premium schedules, collateral arrangements, and a transaction-level funds-flow diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected activity involves high-value cross-border wires, multiple currencies, related-party reinsurance, or payment corridors involving higher-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the reinsurance program, underwriting policy, territory and sanctions matrix, expected monthly transaction volumes, counterparties and countries, payment-purpose taxonomy, sample invoices and bordereaux, claims-payment controls, dual-approval matrix, sanctions-screening procedure, and escalation protocol for unusual transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The bank cannot distinguish genuine insurance premiums and claims from circular intra-group transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed reinsurance treaties, facultative slips where relevant, insured-group policy documentation, actuarial pricing support, premium and claims bordereaux, loss-adjustment evidence, reserve calculations, related-party pricing analysis, transfer-pricing policy, and reconciliations between contracts, ledger entries, bank movements, and regulatory returns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments may involve sanctioned persons, sanctioned territories, politically exposed persons, or restricted dual-use sectors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide group-wide sanctions and PEP policies, screening-tool methodology, screening evidence, beneficial-owner and counterparty certifications, country-risk approvals, senior-management escalations, contractual sanctions clauses, payment-blocking procedures, and documented no-obligation-to-pay analysis where a restriction is identified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The institution is newly formed, has limited French substance, or has directors and signatories resident outside France.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the registered-office agreement, French management and compliance responsibilities, organization chart, service-provider agreements, board minutes, local telephone and correspondence details, tax registration evidence, regulatory correspondence, business continuity plan, and explanation of why France is the operating and supervisory location.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The bank identifies potential tax-evasion, beneficial-ownership, or reporting risk under CRS, FATCA, DAC6, or French tax rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide French tax identification details, CRS entity classification, FATCA status and GIIN where applicable, tax-residency self-certifications, W-8 or W-9 forms where relevant, intercompany transaction schedule, tax-adviser memorandum, transfer-pricing documentation, and a record-retention and reporting-control policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requested accounts appear intended to hold technical provisions or collateral without a clear custody and segregation framework.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the investment and liquidity policy, Solvency II prudent-person framework, asset-liability management report, approved custodian arrangement, collateral-control agreement, segregation and reconciliation procedures, authorized investment list, counterparty limits, and evidence that operating cash is separated from technical-provision and collateral assets.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route capital through an EU-authorized credit institution to an account opened in the exact legal name of the French SAS. For incorporation, use a French capital-deposit or capital-escrow account and instruct the remitter to state the legal basis and purpose, such as paid-in share capital, share premium, shareholder loan, or subordinated capital, without combining distinct instruments. The payment message should identify the shareholder, recipient legal name, French registration number where available, ultimate beneficial owner, and purpose; use the bank's applicable SEPA or SWIFT purpose and regulatory coding rather than inventing a code. Obtain the bank's source-of-funds approval before remittance, retain MT103 or equivalent payment evidence, and reconcile the receipt to the shareholder resolution, subscription agreement, capital table, and notarial or incorporation file. Release of escrow funds should follow registration and production of the updated Kbis extract. Shareholder loans, hybrid instruments, collateral funding, and funds supporting Solvency II own funds require separate documentation, arm's-length terms, accounting classification, regulatory eligibility analysis, and possible ACPR notification or approval. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated group entities, anonymous virtual-asset channels, or an offshore EMI lacking verified EU authorization.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary cross-border commercial payments, use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT customer credit transfers, normally MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. Each payment should contain accurate originator, beneficiary, bank, invoice or treaty reference, purpose, currency, and underlying-contract information. For reinsurance premiums and claims, retain the treaty, bordereau, invoice, claims file, reserve approval, sanctions clearance, and beneficiary verification. Commercial letters of credit may be used for genuine goods or service transactions but are not a substitute for evidence supporting insurance or intra-group transfers; documentary credits should be issued or confirmed by an acceptable bank under applicable ICC rules, with independent trade-document review. Use separate payment workflows for premiums received, claims paid, collateral movements, operating expenses, taxes, dividends, and intercompany loans. Apply maker-checker approval, sanctions screening before release, beneficiary-change call-back controls, payment-limit controls, daily bank reconciliation, liquidity forecasting, and exception reporting. Confirm whether a transaction triggers French, EU, Banque de France, customs, statistical, tax, or prudential reporting before execution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts for documented foreign-currency premium, claims, operating, or investment exposures, subject to board-approved limits, counterparty eligibility, valuation, collateral, and Solvency II risk-management controls.

Non-deliverable forwards only where legally available for the relevant currency and economically justified by a documented exposure; the settlement currency, benchmark, fixing source, counterparty status, model valuation, collateral terms, and sanctions analysis must be approved in advance.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for identified balance-sheet or funding exposures, with ISDA or equivalent master documentation, collateral terms, close-out provisions, counterparty limits, independent valuation, and regulatory reporting controls.
Exchange-traded or cleared currency futures and options through an eligible clearing member, subject to margin, liquidity, basis-risk, accounting, and collateral controls.

Currency options or collars for defined insurance cash-flow exposures, subject to a prohibition on speculative or unbounded-risk structures unless specifically approved under the undertaking's risk appetite and prudential framework.

Hedging must be demonstrably connected to the reinsurance undertaking's liabilities, assets, funding, or operational exposures. It must not impair technical-provision security, eligible-own-funds requirements, liquidity coverage, asset segregation, or the prudent-person principle. Derivative documentation should address EMIR clearing, margin, trade-reporting, risk-mitigation, and bilateral-counterparty requirements where applicable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of statutory financial statements and allocation of results (shareholder decision taken per the SAS bylaws, recorded in the corporate minute book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate governance act of the SAS shareholders; not filed with the Government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (calendar-year entities: by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government pecuniary penalty; failure to approve the annual accounts within 6 months blocks the mandatory deposit at the Commercial Registry, exposes management to civil liability, and may prompt ACPR prudential corrective measures for the licensed captive reinsurer

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt des comptes annuels — deposit of annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, notes, management report and statutory auditors' report) with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of fiscal year-end and no later than 1 month after shareholder approval (calendar-year entities: by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court fine of up to €1,500 for natural persons / €7,500 for legal entities; coercive astreinte of up to €1,500 per month; repeated omission triggers formal notice and administrative radiation (strike-off) from the Register of Companies, with consequent loss of legal personality and director disqualification risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Integrated corporate income tax return (liassez fiscale — Form 2065 series) including the registered financial statements and insurance-specific annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP — Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (French Tax Authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second business day after 1 May for calendar-year accounting periods (typically 3 May); for off-calendar fiscal years, by the adjusted schedule announced by DGFiP within 6 months of the balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10%, increased to 40% in bad faith and 80% for fraud or organized scheme; monthly late-payment interest of 0.40%; compulsory tax assessment following formal notice; publication of penalties and potential tax lien over corporate assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Solvency II annual prudential and public reporting package for the captive reinsurance undertaking (annual QRTs, Regular Supervisory Report RSR, and public Solvency and Financial Condition Report SFCR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: ACPR — Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority, Banque de France)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual QRTs and RSR within 14 weeks after fiscal year-end; SFCR publicly disclosed within the same 14-week window; quarterly QRTs within 6 weeks after each quarter-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: ACPR disciplinary sanctions: formal notice, warning, reprimand, financial penalty of up to €4 million or 10% of annual turnover (Article L.612-41 CMF), restriction or withdrawal of the reinsurance authorization, and publication of the sanction decision

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO declaration maintenance (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs — DBE) and rectification of the beneficial ownership register in case of share transfers or control changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (filed at the commercial registry and transmitted to DGFiP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any beneficial ownership change; no standalone annual deadline — confirmation of unchanged UBO data is embedded in the annual accounts deposit filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalties for legal representatives of up to 6 months' imprisonment and €18,750 fine (Article L.561-8 of the Monetary and Financial Code); greffe refusal of subsequent filings; court-ordered injunction with coercive fine; strike-off risk for persistent non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all licensed captive reinsurance undertakings under the French Insurance Code regardless of size: appointment of at least one statutory auditor (Commissaire aux comptes) and one alternate is a prudential licensing condition; the general SAS size thresholds (two of three: €4M balance sheet total, €8M net turnover, 50 employees) do not apply to this regulated entity
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under ANC Regulation 2014-03, supplemented by ANC Regulation 2015-11 for individual insurance/reinsurance accounts and the Plan Comptable des Assurances; statutory legal-entity accounts are prepared under the Code de commerce and Code des assurances; prudential returns follow the Solvency II / EIOPA QRT framework; consolidated IFRS is permitted for groups but the French legal entity accounts remain under French GAAP

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a separate annual UBO re-confirmation form. The beneficial owners declaration filed with the Commercial Registry must be updated within 30 days after any change in ownership or control; annually, the deposit of annual accounts requires confirmation that the declared beneficial ownership remains accurate, and any share transfer must be reported within the same 30-day window.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders (Registre des titres et des transferts)
Register of Corporate Decisions and Minutes (Registre des décisions et procès-verbaux)
Minute Book of Shareholder Meetings (Livre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$300 – US$6,500 per year (basic commercial domiciliation from 120–360 EUR/year; full corporate secretarial and registered-agent mandate for a regulated captive SAS from 2,000–6,000 EUR/year)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$12,000 – US$35,000 per year (statutory audit of a regulated captive reinsurance entity, including Solvency II reporting review and SFCR validation)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax. A 3.3% social contribution on corporate income may apply to companies with annual turnover of at least EUR 7.63 million and corporate income tax exceeding EUR 763,000, producing an effective rate of approximately 25.825% before temporary or sector-specific surcharges.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% corporate income tax rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory ownership, turnover and paid-up-capital conditions. Tax credits may apply for qualifying research, innovation, audiovisual, film, apprenticeship and other activities. France generally does not provide a standard corporate tax holiday for a captive reinsurance company. Insurance and reinsurance activities remain subject to prudential authorization and sector-specific taxation rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French tax administration's professional portal EDI-TDFC or the impots.gouv.fr professional account. The return is accompanied, as applicable, by Forms 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD, 2059-A-SD to 2059-G-SD, and the relevant simplified or full tax-package schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return, with quarterly corporate income tax instalments generally payable during the fiscal year and a final balance payment after year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the return is generally due on the second business day following 1 May of the following year. For a year-end other than 31 December, the return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. The final corporate income tax balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the balance is generally due by 15 May. Electronic-filing administrative extensions may apply under current filing-calendar rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, French SIREN number, registered office, tax office, fiscal year beginning and ending dates, legal form as SAS, and the applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not entered as the taxpayer unless it operates through a French permanent establishment. The French SAS reports its own French tax residence, SIREN and registered office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss adjusted for French tax add-backs, deductions, exempt items, non-deductible expenses, depreciation restrictions, provisions, tax credits and other fiscal adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only items attributable to the French SAS. Do not deduct foreign shareholder expenses unless they are properly charged, commercially justified, arm's-length and supported by documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at the applicable rate, including any applicable reduced-rate portion, social contribution, credits, instalments and balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident owner does not change the SAS's domestic corporate income tax computation. Treaty relief generally applies to cross-border payments, not to the SAS's ordinary French taxable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting result to taxable result, including permanent differences, temporary differences, non-deductible charges, exempt income and tax-specific adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose related-party charges, financing costs, management fees, reinsurance premiums and claims-related adjustments consistently with statutory accounts and transfer-pricing support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses available for carryforward or, where conditions are met, carryback, together with losses utilized in the current period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain a schedule separating French tax losses from foreign or shareholder-level losses. Changes in activity or ownership can restrict the use of carried-forward losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable profit between ordinary result, capital gains and other tax categories where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not classify ordinary underwriting or investment income as exempt foreign income merely because the recipient or counterparty is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2059-A-SD to 2059-G-SD, capital gains and participation information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains, long-term gains, participation disposals, provisions, depreciation and other items required by the tax package.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French exemptions or reduced regimes only where statutory holding, accounting and substance conditions are satisfied and documentary evidence is retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of specified non-deductible expenses, including certain luxury, penalty, gift, interest and excess remuneration items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party charges, shareholder benefits and penalties must not be presented as deductible operating expenses without a specific French tax basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, foreign tax credits where available, instalments paid, withholding taxes and the resulting amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits require a French legal basis, proof of foreign tax paid and compliance with applicable treaty limitations. Do not claim shareholder-level foreign tax credits in the SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information required by applicable French related-party, group, controlled-entity, country-by-country and transfer-pricing reporting rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report material transactions with non-resident affiliates, including premiums, retrocession, claims handling, financing, guarantees, investment management and service fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, subject to statutory exceptions and escalation. Late payment of tax generally bears interest at 0.20% per month, calculated under the French Tax Code. Deliberate, abusive or fraudulent conduct can trigger 40% or 80% tax increases, criminal tax-fraud prosecution, denial of deductions, and assessment of withholding taxes. Inaccurate transfer-pricing documentation can support a reassessment and a penalty generally linked to the greater of the reassessed amount or a statutory minimum, subject to applicable rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2572-SD, corporate income tax balance and instalment settlement, filed and paid electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional account or approved electronic payment channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly instalments and annual final settlement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Corporate income tax instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, subject to fiscal-year and tax-calendar adjustments. The final balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax assessed for the relevant fiscal year, reduced by eligible credits and prior instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS's assessed liability only. Foreign parent tax payments are not instalments of the SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Instalments already paid for the fiscal year and any credit carried forward or refund requested.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the tax account before requesting a refund, particularly where the SAS has received foreign-source income or withholding credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance remaining after credits and instalments, including any applicable social contribution or surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made electronically from an approved account. Manual payment methods can create filing or payment non-compliance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may trigger a 5% payment surcharge in addition to late-payment interest, subject to statutory exceptions. Repeated non-payment can lead to enforced collection, bank-account seizure, tax liens and director liability in cases involving serious mismanagement or fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The standard French withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders is generally 25%, subject to treaty relief, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief and statutory exemptions. Dividends paid by a French SAS to a qualifying EU parent may be exempt where the ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, anti-abuse and beneficial-ownership conditions are satisfied. French resident individual shareholder distributions are subject to separate personal-income withholding rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide a valid certificate of tax residence issued by its competent foreign tax authority and evidence of beneficial ownership, entitlement to treaty benefits and satisfaction of any limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse conditions. French administrative Forms 5000 and 5001 are commonly used for dividend relief; Forms 5000 and 5002 generally relate to interest; Forms 5000 and 5003 generally relate to royalties. The payer should apply the reduced rate only where the procedural conditions are met, retain the evidence, report the payment and withholding, and pay the tax through the required French filing channel. If relief cannot be applied at source, the recipient may seek a refund from the French tax administration. Treaty rates must be verified against the treaty in force with the recipient's jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on royalties and similar payments to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to treaty reduction, EU rules where applicable, and statutory exclusions. Ordinary interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax, but exceptions can apply, including payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions or certain anti-abuse and special-regime situations. Treaty rates vary and commonly reduce royalty withholding to approximately 0% to 15% and interest withholding to 0% to 10%. Payments must be reviewed for beneficial ownership, treaty residence, associated-enterprise pricing, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation and recharacterization as a dividend.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million threshold for the principal French full transfer-pricing documentation obligation, generally based on turnover or gross assets, or where the French entity is associated with an entity meeting the statutory threshold. A country-by-country report generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Entities below the full-documentation threshold must still apply the arm's-length principle and produce supporting information upon request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no separate Cayman-style general Economic Substance Regulations regime. Nevertheless, French anti-abuse doctrine, the abuse-of-law rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, permanent-establishment principles, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules and general arm's-length requirements require genuine commercial substance. A captive reinsurance SAS should maintain French governance, appropriately qualified personnel or demonstrable outsourced capabilities, risk-management systems, underwriting authority, actuarial support, claims oversight, capital and solvency resources, board minutes, decision-making evidence and a commercially coherent risk-retention and retrocession policy. Reinsurance activity also requires authorization and continuing prudential compliance with the French Insurance Code, ACPR supervision and applicable Solvency II requirements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Writing, accepting or retroceding reinsurance business in France without the required authorization, or conducting regulated insurance activity outside the authorized classes and business plan.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative measures may include injunctions, business restrictions, authorization withdrawal, fines and liquidation proceedings. Unauthorized insurance activity may also constitute a criminal offence under the French Insurance Code, with imprisonment and corporate and individual fines potentially reaching statutory maximums of approximately EUR 75,000 for an individual and EUR 375,000 for a legal entity, subject to the applicable provision and facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face personal criminal prosecution, civil damages, regulatory disqualification and asset claims. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be ordered in criminal proceedings; imprisonment is possible where the statutory offence and culpability are established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing premiums, investment income or related-party payments; fabricating claims or expenses; submitting materially false tax returns; or intentionally using sham arrangements to reduce French tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, 40% or 80% tax increases, confiscatory measures and criminal tax-fraud penalties. Aggravated tax fraud can result in imprisonment of up to seven years and fines of up to EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur criminal liability, civil tax liability for fraudulent conduct, management bans and asset seizure. A travel ban or pre-trial detention may be ordered by a court where legally justified; neither is automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Overpricing retrocession, management, actuarial, investment-management or financing charges; underpricing intra-group services; shifting underwriting profit without functional support; or failing to document related-party pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment under the arm's-length principle, withholding tax exposure, interest, penalties, documentation-related fines and possible 40% or 80% increases where deliberate abuse or fraud is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for intentional fraud, serious mismanagement or participation in sham transactions. Ordinary transfer-pricing adjustment alone does not automatically pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal French SAS with no genuine underwriting decisions, employees or outsourced control framework, while profits are contractually or practically directed to a foreign affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions, denial of treaty benefits, permanent-establishment findings, transfer-pricing adjustments, abuse-of-law penalties, withholding tax assessments and possible authorization or prudential sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable where they knowingly orchestrate sham arrangements, conceal beneficial ownership or misuse company assets. Civil restitution and asset seizure may follow; imprisonment requires a separately proven criminal offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties or other taxable amounts to non-residents without withholding, applying a treaty rate without valid residence documentation, or failing to report and remit withheld tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French payer may be assessed for the unremitted withholding tax, late-payment interest and applicable surcharges. Treaty relief may be denied where residence, beneficial ownership, anti-abuse or procedural requirements are not satisfied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur liability for deliberate withholding-tax evasion or misuse of withheld funds. Criminal exposure is fact-dependent; automatic personal liability does not arise from an innocent administrative error.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify policyholders, cedants, retrocessionaires or beneficial owners; accepting opaque premium flows; ignoring sanctions screening; or facilitating money laundering, terrorist financing or sanctions evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACPR or other competent-authority enforcement may include reprimands, injunctions, business restrictions, substantial administrative fines, authorization withdrawal and publication of sanctions. Money-laundering and terrorist-financing conduct may trigger criminal prosecution, confiscation and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face personal criminal liability for knowing participation, facilitation or serious compliance failures. Asset freezing, confiscation, judicial control, travel restrictions and imprisonment may apply when ordered under the relevant criminal or sanctions regime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False claims, accounting fraud and reserve manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fabricating insured losses, overstating technical provisions, concealing adverse development, manipulating claims files or producing false statutory accounts and solvency information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restatement, prudential capital measures, regulatory sanctions, tax consequences, damages to counterparties and criminal penalties for fraud, forgery or false accounting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, senior officers, actuaries and other responsible persons may face personal civil and criminal liability, professional bans, confiscation and imprisonment where the elements of the relevant offence are proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper profit distribution and capital impairment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends from non-distributable reserves, distributing while statutory accounts do not support distributable profit, or extracting funds that impair solvency or creditor protection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful dividends, shareholder and director liability, corporate-law penalties, insolvency claims and potential criminal sanctions for unlawful distribution or misuse of corporate assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may owe restitution and damages, face management disqualification and be exposed to insolvency contribution claims. Imprisonment or travel restrictions require a qualifying criminal offence and judicial order.
